frames.reason: Alignment: all four captures show ORE 890, GAS 182, SUPPLY 23/30, CLOCK 00:12 and Vanguard 10 selected, 100/100, -57/49, IDLE. Objects, rings, bars, crater and the lit/shade boundary sit at identical pixels, and repeats within each arm look identical by eye. I saw no hostile unit, order marker, debris or animation difference, so the differences are rendering and HUD only. Visible gains: the shade floor lifts from dark charcoal-teal to mid blue-grey and the lit area from dim taupe to warm khaki. That reads closer to the soft light-grey, warm-lit/cool-shade ground of the Unreal L9 panels than BEFORE's crushed murk. Grid, crater warp and base shadows stay legible in the lifted shade. No new flat or clipped white patch (barracks roof stripe x582-615,y385-412 and dome caps keep their shape), and crystals and teal accents are more vivid. Contact: the dark pedestals under core and barracks and the harvester bases (x70-130,y285-345) still read, if anything more clearly on the lighter floor, and nothing floats. Building rings are visibly bolder bright cyan with dark edging. Infantry arcs look equal or brighter. Bars keep extents and fill/track splits: paler mint fill, black tracks more distinct. The pool is lighter aqua with a crisp edge and its dark lower-right lip retained. Trade-offs, not regressions: the lit/shade floor step is flatter than BEFORE but the boundary still reads clearly. The map-edge wedge appears lighter and warmer than the adjacent shade floor in PINNED (darker in BEFORE) but is still distinct by missing grid. HUD: every label, button and minimap element is present, at higher contrast on near-black. The new hint strip covers only floor/grid, no cue visible BEFORE. No banding, grain, halo or ghost edge seen at native size. The gain is mostly tonal (lift and curve), not sky or specular, and the contrast watch stays open.

frames.reason: Alignment: all four captures show ORE 1,590, GAS 334, SUPPLY 23/30, CLOCK 01:01 and Vanguard 10 selected, 100/100, -21/9, IDLE. Every object, ring, bar, minimap marker and the lit-band outline coincide, and repeats within each arm match by eye. There is no hostile unit, order or target marker, combat or debris in any frame, so none can be compared. Shade floor and the top-left void lift from near-black charcoal to blue-grey and the lit band to warm khaki. Grid and base shadows stay legible and I saw no clipped patch. Core and barracks keep at least the same facet and tonal separation, with a more vivid teal roof inset, dome and crystals. Contact pedestals, harvester bases (x405-445,y360-405) and dark bases persist on the lighter floor. Rings on core, barracks, sentinel, tank and tower are bolder with dark edging. The infantry cluster keeps bodies, dark chests and cyan slits, arcs and bars at the same positions, separated from the lighter floor by hue and dark facets. Bars keep extents and splits, with the dark tracks (core, blue tank) more distinct. HUD is complete and higher contrast. The hint strip covers only floor/grid: no unit, ring, bar, button, minimap, PAUSE or pool. The pool sliver is lighter and sits below it. Same tonal-only gain as performance, no confirmed regression, and the contrast watch stays open.

reason: Two-pose subset only. In both poses AFTER is visibly closer to the Unreal L9 tonal character. Cool shade is lifted against warm lit ground, shade and contact detail is retained, and I saw no new clipped highlight. HUD text and controls, rings, bars, units, buildings, crystals, pool and minimap are all present and equal or stronger than BEFORE. The hint strip hides no gameplay cue in either pose. I found no confirmed readability, contact or target regression and no hard contradiction. The gain is mainly exposure and tone; these poses have no sky or specular highlights, so those L9 aspects are unjudged. The lit/shade floor step is flatter than BEFORE but the boundary stays clear. The contrast watch remains open (see contrastWatchDecision). This subset does not establish whole-kit IMPROVEMENT, and the temporal exposure criterion is unverified.
limitations: Read-only visual review: no zoom beyond native frames, no pixel diff or measurement, coordinates by eye. The viewer downsampled both sheets, so I judged from the raw repeats: all eight opened once, plus a native re-read of the four run-1 frames for the watch. Static endpoints only. Exposure settling, pumping or flicker (the PRD temporal criterion), adaptation, shimmer of thin rings and grid in motion, FPS, audio and unseen gameplay are NOT verified; matching repeats show endpoint repeatability only. Neither pose has hostile units, order or target markers, damage feedback, a drag-select box or low-health infantry bars (all infantry bars appear full). Enemy-colour readability, order cues and infantry partial-fill are therefore unassessed; only the two-tone building bars show fill/track splits. No sky is visible. I judged L9 proximity on tonal range, highlight handling, shade colour, depth and contact, using only the Unreal panels of the mixed boards and not the ThreeNative panels. The hint strip covers only floor/grid here; what it dims in other poses is unassessed. The watch metrics come from AI-attack only and were not re-measured on these poses. Panels changed from teal to near-black, matching the stated PINNED HUD intent. I treat that as readability-neutral or positive, not as L9 credit. No benefit is credited to the resolutionScale pin; BEFORE and PINNED look equally sharp. The performance PINNED repeats are the reused preflight frames; the rts-attack PINNED frames are fresh.
contrastWatchDecision:
No WHOLE bar, ring or infantry cue is confirmed weaker in either pose, so actualCueRegression is false, but the watch is not closed by this enum.

Performance (1920x1080), both PINNED repeats:
- Rings: core x252-457,y262-413; barracks arcs x500-650,y430-475; building x375-473,y118-180; tank x557-622,y190-220; blue tank x718-770,y190-215; left tower x0-45,y360-410. All are continuous with identical geometry, and the building rings are visibly bolder bright cyan with a dark edge.
- Infantry arcs x683-818,y290-345 look equal or brighter.
- Bars: core x300-408,y262-268; building x370-478,y98-104; tank x563-617,y157-160; barracks x523-632,y360-364; blue tank dark bar x718-770,y157-160; infantry bars x676-795,y224-290. All keep extent, crisp ends and fill/track splits. The fill is paler mint than BEFORE's sage, but the black tracks stand out more on the lifted floor.
- Infantry x675-825,y224-345 keep dark chests and cyan slits and stay separated from the lighter tan floor by hue and dark facets.

rts-attack (1280x720) shows the same for the core ring and bar (x526-662,y347-448), barracks (x685-800,y400-490), the sentinel, tank and tower rings, and the cluster x805-905,y320-400.

Remaining uncertainty, not confirmed: where pale mint bars sit against the palest infantry faces, lightness separation is plausibly smaller than BEFORE. The AI-attack metrics show the sampled bar L* step 25.87 -> 20.75 and Y ratio 2.829 -> 2.021, with absolute Y separation rising. The ring-edge sample drops from about 15 to 8.8-11.1 L* in repeat 2 and repeat 1 respectively, and its absolute Y separation falls in repeat 2 only, while RGB distance rises. I did not re-measure these on my poses. At native size I could not see any bar or arc as fainter. The dark backing (clear as dark rims on the big rings and as black tracks) and the larger absolute separation offset it. I cannot resolve the 1-3 px underlay separately from the foreground on the infantry bars. No threshold exists, and metrics are not proof of global readability.
